plan: Isaiah 58:1-14; Isaiah 59:1-21; Isaiah 60:1-22; Isaiah 61:1-11; Isaiah 62:1-12; Isaiah 63:1-6, 7-14

readings.title: A Rebuke of Hypocritical Fasting
readings.subtitle: God questions the motives behind Israel's religious observances.
readings.text: <dq>“Cry aloud, do not spare. Lift up your voice like the shophar. Declare to <dn>My</dn> people their transgression, and the house of Ya‛aqoḇ their sins.</dq> [2] <dq>“Yet they seek <dn>Me</dn> day by day, and delight to know <dn>My</dn> ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and did not forsake the right-ruling of their <dn>Elohim</dn>. They ask of <dn>Me</dn> rulings of righteousness, they delight in drawing near to <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>They say, ‘Why have we fasted, and <dn>You</dn> have not seen? Why have we afflicted <dn>את</dn> our beings, and <dn>You</dn> took no note?’ “Look, in the day of your fasting you find pleasure, and drive on all your labourers.</dq> [4] <dq>“Look, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wrongness. <dn>You</dn> do not fast as you do this day, to make your voice heard on high.</dq> [5] <dq>“Is it a fast that <dn>I</dn> have chosen, a day for a man to afflict <dn>את</dn> his being? Is it to bow down his head like a bulrush, and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? Do you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?</dq>

readings.title: The Nature of a True Fast
readings.subtitle: Acts of justice, mercy, and compassion are the fast that pleases God.
readings.text: <dq>“Is this not the fast that <dn>I</dn> have chosen: to loosen the tight cords of wrongness, to undo the bands of the yoke, to exempt the oppressed, and to break off every yoke?</dq> [7] <dq>“Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and that you bring to your house the poor who are cast out; when you see the naked, and cover him, and not hide yourself from your own flesh?</dq> [8] <dq>“Then your light would break forth like the morning, your healing spring forth speedily. And your righteousness shall go before you, the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would be your rear guard.</dq> [9] <dq>“Then, when you call, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would answer; when you cry, <dn>He</dn> would say, ‘Here <dn>I</dn> am.’ “If you take away the yoke from your midst, the pointing of the finger, and the speaking of unrighteousness,</dq> [10] <dq>if you extend your being to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted being, then your light shall dawn in the darkness, and your darkness be as noon.</dq> [11] <dq>“Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would guide you continually, and satisfy your being in drought, and strengthen your bones. And you shall be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail.</dq> [12] <dq>“And those from among you shall build the old waste places. <dn>You</dn> shall raise up the foundations of many generations. And you would be called the Repairer of the Breach, the Restorer of Streets to Dwell In.</dq>

readings.title: Blessings for Honoring the Sabbath
readings.subtitle: Delighting in God's set-apart day brings exaltation and inheritance.
readings.text: <dq>“If you do turn back your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on <dn>My</dn> set-apart day, and shall call the Sabbath ’a delight,’ the set-apart day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> ‘esteemed,’ and shall esteem it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words,</dq> [14] <dq>then you shall delight yourself in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> shall cause you to ride on the heights of the earth, and feed you with the inheritance of Ya‛aqoḇ your father. For the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken!”</dq>

readings.title: Sin, the Great Separator
readings.subtitle: The people's iniquities, not God's inability, have created a barrier.
readings.text: [Isaiah 59:1] Look, the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not become too short to save, nor <dn>His</dn> ear too heavy to hear. [2] But your crookednesses have separated you from your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And your sins have hidden <dn>His</dn> face from you, from hearing. [3] For your hands have been defiled with blood, and your fingers with crookedness; your lips have spoken falsehood, your tongue mutters unrighteousness. [4] No one calls for righteousness, and no one pleads for truth. They trust in emptiness and speak worthlessness; they conceive trouble and bring forth wickedness. [5] They have hatched adders’ eggs and they weave the spider’s web. Whoever eats their eggs dies, and when one is broken an adder is hatched. [6] Their webs do not become garments, nor do they cover themselves with their works. Their works are works of wickedness, and a deed of violence is in their hands. [7] Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of wickedness, wasting and ruin are in their highways. [8] The way of peace they have not known, and there is no right-ruling in their ways. They have made crooked paths for themselves, whoever treads in them shall not know peace.

readings.title: A Confession of National Sin
readings.subtitle: The people acknowledge their blindness, transgression, and the absence of truth.
readings.text: [Isaiah 59:9] Therefore right-ruling has been far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We look for light, but there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in thick darkness! [10] We feel for the wall like the blind, and we feel as without eyes. At noon we stumble as at twilight, in deserted places, like the dead. [11] All of us growl like bears, and moan sadly like doves. We look for right-ruling, but there is none; for deliverance, but it is far from us. [12] For our transgressions have increased before <dn>You</dn>, and our sins witnessed against us. For our transgressions are with us, and as for our crookednesses, we know them: [13] transgressing, and being untrue to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and turning away from our <dn>Elohim</dn>, speaking oppression and apostasy, conceiving and pondering words of falsehood from the heart. [14] And right-ruling is driven back, and righteousness stands far off. For truth has fallen in the street, and right is unable to enter.

readings.title: The Divine Warrior Intervenes
readings.subtitle: Seeing no intercessor, God Himself puts on armor to bring salvation and a new covenant.
readings.text: [Isaiah 59:15] And the truth is lacking, and whoever turns away from evil makes himself a prey. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw, and it displeased <dn>Him</dn> that there was no right-ruling. [16] And <dn>He</dn> saw that there was no man, and was astonished that there was no intercessor. So <dn>His</dn> own arm saved for <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> righteousness upheld him. [17] And <dn>He</dn> put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of deliverance on <dn>His</dn> head. And <dn>He</dn> put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and wrapped <dn>Himself</dn> with ardour as a mantle. [18] According to their deeds, so <dn>He</dn> repays, wrath to <dn>His</dn> adversaries, recompense to <dn>His</dn> enemies. <dn>He</dn> repays recompense to the coastlands. [19] And they shall fear <dn>את</dn> the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the west, and <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> esteem from the rising of the sun, when distress comes like a flood, the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drives at it. [20] <dq>“And the Redeemer shall come to Tsiyon, and to those turning from transgression in Ya‛aqoḇ,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [21] <dq>“As for <dn>Me</dn>, this is <dn>My</dn> covenant with them,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: <dq>“<dn>My</dn> Spirit that is upon you, and <dn>My</dn> Words that <dn>I</dn> have put in your mouth, shall not be withdrawn from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your descendants, nor from the mouth of your descendants’ descendants,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“from this time and forever.”</dq>

readings.title: Arise, Shine, for Your Light Has Come
readings.subtitle: God declares that His glory will rise upon Zion, drawing the nations to its light.
readings.text: <dq>“Arise, shine, for your light has come! And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has risen upon you.</dq> [2] <dq>“For look, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness the peoples. But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> arises over you, and <dn>His</dn> esteem is seen upon you.</dq> [3] <dq>“And the nations shall come to your light, and sovereigns to the brightness of your rising.</dq> [4] <dq>“Lift up your eyes all around and see: all of them have gathered, they have come to you; your sons come from afar, and your daughters are supported on the side.</dq> [5] <dq>“Then you shall see and be bright, and your heart shall throb and swell, for the wealth of the sea is turned to you, the riches of the nations come to you.</dq> [6] <dq>“A stream of camels cover your land, the dromedaries of Miḏyan and Ěphah; all those from Sheḇa come, bearing gold and incense, and proclaiming the praises of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>“All the flocks of Qěḏar are gathered to you, the rams of Neḇayoth serve you; they come up for acceptance on <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place, and <dn>I</dn> embellish <dn>My</dn> esteemed House.</dq>

readings.title: The Nations Serve Zion
readings.subtitle: Foreigners and their kings will rebuild the city and bring their wealth.
readings.text: <dq>“Who are these who fly like a cloud, and like doves to their windows?</dq> [9] <dq>“Because the coastlands wait for <dn>Me</dn>, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, to the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and to the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, because <dn>He</dn> has adorned you.</dq> [10] <dq>“And the sons of foreigners shall build your walls, and their sovereigns serve you. For in <dn>My</dn> wrath <dn>I</dn> have stricken you, but in <dn>My</dn> delight <dn>I</dn> shall have compassion on you.</dq> [11] <dq>“And your gates shall be open continually, they are not shut day or night, to bring to you the wealth of the nations, and their sovereigns in procession.</dq> [12] <dq>“For the nation and the reign that do not serve you shall perish, and those nations shall be utterly laid waste.</dq> [13] <dq>“The esteem of Leḇanon shall come to you, cypress, pine, and the box tree together, to embellish the place of <dn>My</dn> set-apart place. And <dn>I</dn> shall make the place of <dn>My</dn> feet esteemed.</dq> [14] <dq>“And the sons of those who afflicted you come bowing to you, and all those who despised you shall bow themselves at the soles of your feet. And they shall call you: City of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Tsiyon of the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl.</dq>

readings.title: Zion's Everlasting Light
readings.subtitle: God Himself will be the city's light, bringing peace, righteousness, and unending prosperity.
readings.text: <dq>“Instead of you being forsaken and hated, so that no one passes through you, <dn>I</dn> shall make you an everlasting excellence, a joy of many generations.</dq> [16] <dq>“And you shall suck the milk of the nations, and shall suckle the breast of sovereigns. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, your Saviour and your Redeemer, am the Mighty One of Ya‛aqoḇ.</dq> [17] <dq>“Instead of bronze <dn>I</dn> bring gold, and instead of iron <dn>I</dn> bring silver, and bronze instead of wood, and iron instead of stones. And <dn>I</dn> shall make your officers peace, and your magistrates righteousness.</dq> [18] <dq>“Violence shall no longer be heard in your land, neither wasting nor ruin within your borders. And you shall call your walls Deliverance, and your gates Praise.</dq> [19] <dq>“No longer is the sun your light by day, nor does the moon give light to you for brightness, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be to you an everlasting light, and your <dn>Elohim</dn> your comeliness.</dq> [20] <dq>“No longer does your sun go down, nor your moon withdraw itself, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning shall be ended.</dq> [21] <dq>“And your people, all of them righteous, shall inherit the earth forever – a branch of <dn>My</dn> planting, a work of <dn>My</dn> hands, to be adorned.</dq> [22] <dq>“The little shall become a thousand, and the small one a strong nation. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, shall hasten it in its time.”</dq>

readings.title: The Mission of the Anointed One
readings.subtitle: The Spirit empowers the Messiah to bring good news, healing, and liberty.
readings.text: [Isaiah 61:1] <dq>The Spirit of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is upon <dn>Me</dn>, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has anointed <dn>Me</dn> to bring good news to the meek. <dn>He</dn> has sent <dn>Me</dn> to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, and the opening of the prison to those who are bound,</dq> [2] <dq>to proclaim the acceptable year of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the day of vengeance of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to comfort all who mourn,</dq> [3] <dq>to appoint unto those who mourn in Tsiyon: to give them embellishment for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness. And they shall be called trees of righteousness, a planting of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to be adorned.</dq>

readings.title: The Joy of the Redeemed
readings.subtitle: Israel will be restored as priests, receiving a double portion and an everlasting covenant.
readings.text: [Isaiah 61:4] And they shall rebuild the old ruins, raise up the former wastes. And they shall restore the ruined cities, the wastes of many generations. [5] And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the foreigner be your ploughmen and your vinedressers. [6] But you shall be called, ‘Priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,’ ‘Servants of our <dn>Elohim</dn>’ shall be said of you. <dn>You</dn> shall consume the strength of the nations, and boast in their esteem. [7] Instead of your shame and reproach, they rejoice a second time in their portion. Therefore they take possession a second time in their land, everlasting joy is theirs. [8] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, love right-ruling; <dn>I</dn> hate robbery for ascending offering. And <dn>I</dn> shall give their reward in truth, and make an everlasting covenant with them.</dq> [9] <dq>“And their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples. All who see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed.”</dq> [10] <dn>I</dn> greatly rejoice in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>my</dn> being exults in <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>. For <dn>He</dn> has put garments of deliverance on <dn>me</dn>, <dn>He</dn> has covered <dn>me</dn> with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels. [11] For as the earth brings forth its bud, as the garden causes the seed to shoot up, so the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> causes righteousness and praise to shoot up before all the nations!

readings.title: Zion's New Name
readings.subtitle: No longer 'Forsaken,' she will be called 'My Delight Is in Her' and 'Married.'
readings.text: [Isaiah 62:1] <dq>For Tsiyon’s sake <dn>I</dn> am not silent, and for Yerushalayim’s sake <dn>I</dn> do not rest, until her righteousness goes forth as brightness, and her deliverance as a lamp that burns.</dq> [2] And the nations shall see your righteousness, and all sovereigns your esteem. And you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> designates. [3] And you shall be a crown of comeliness in the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and a royal head-dress in the hand of your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [4] No longer are you called “Forsaken,” and no longer is your land called “Deserted.” But you shall be called “Ḥephtsiḇah,” and your land “Married,” for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall delight in you, and your land be married. [5] For as a young man marries a maiden, so shall your sons marry you. And as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your <dn>Elohim</dn> rejoice over you.

readings.title: Watchmen on the Walls
readings.subtitle: A call for constant prayer until God's promises for Jerusalem are fulfilled.
readings.text: [Isaiah 62:6] <dq><dn>I</dn> have set watchmen on your walls, O Yerushalayim, all the day and all the night, continually, who are not silent.</dq> <dn>You</dn> who remember <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, give yourselves no rest, [7] and give <dn>Him</dn> no rest till <dn>He</dn> establishes and till <dn>He</dn> makes <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim a praise in the earth. [8] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn by <dn>His</dn> right hand and by the arm of <dn>His</dn> strength, <dq>“No more do <dn>I</dn> give your grain to be food for your enemies, nor do sons of the foreigner drink your new wine, for which you have laboured;</dq> [9] <dq>but those gathering it shall eat it, and praise <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And those collecting it shall drink it in <dn>My</dn> set-apart courts.”</dq> [10] Pass through, pass through the gates! Prepare the way for the people. Build up, build up the highway! Remove the stones. Lift up a banner for the peoples! [11] See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has proclaimed to the end of the earth: <dq>“Say to the daughter of Tsiyon, ‘See, your deliverance has come; see, <dn>His</dn> reward is with <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> work before <dn>Him</dn>.’ ”</dq> [12] And they shall be called, “The Set-apart People, the Redeemed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And you shall be called, “Sought Out, a City Not Forsaken.”

readings.title: The Warrior from Edom
readings.subtitle: A vision of the divine warrior, stained with the blood of His enemies, treading the winepress of God's wrath alone.
readings.text: [Isaiah 63:1] Who is this coming from Eḏom, with garments of glowing colours from Botsrah, who is robed in splendour, striding forward in the greatness of <dn>His</dn> strength? <dq>“It is <dn>I</dn> who speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”</dq> [2] Why is there red on <dn>Your</dn> raiment, and <dn>Your</dn> garments like one who treads in the winepress? [3] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples no one was with <dn>Me</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> trod them down in <dn>My</dn> displeasure, and <dn>I</dn> trampled them in <dn>My</dn> wrath. Their blood is sprinkled upon <dn>My</dn> garments, and <dn>I</dn> have defiled all <dn>My</dn> raiment.</dq> [4] <dq>“For a day of vengeance is in <dn>My</dn> heart, and the year of <dn>My</dn> redeemed has come.</dq> [5] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> looked, but there was none helping, and <dn>I</dn> was astonished that there was none upholding. So <dn>My</dn> own arm saved for <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>My</dn> wrath upheld <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> trod down peoples in <dn>My</dn> displeasure, and made them drunk in <dn>My</dn> wrath, and brought down their strength to earth.”</dq>

readings.title: A Prayer Recounting God's Faithfulness
readings.subtitle: Remembering God's past mercies, His salvation during the Exodus, and Israel's subsequent rebellion.
readings.text: [Isaiah 63:7] Let me recount the loving-commitments of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the praises of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has done for us, and the great goodness toward the house of Yisra’ěl, which <dn>He</dn> has done for them according to <dn>His</dn> compassion, and according to <dn>His</dn> many loving-commitments. [8] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“They are <dn>My</dn> people, children who do not act falsely.”</dq> And <dn>He</dn> became their Saviour. [9] In all their distress <dn>He</dn> was distressed, and the Messenger of <dn>His</dn> Presence saved them. In <dn>His</dn> love and in <dn>His</dn> compassion <dn>He</dn> redeemed them, and <dn>He</dn> lifted them up and carried them all the days of old. [10] But they rebelled and grieved <dn>His</dn> Set-apart Spirit, so <dn>He</dn> turned against them as an enemy, and <dn>He</dn> fought against them. [11] Then <dn>He</dn> remembered the days of old, Mosheh, <dn>His</dn> people, “Where is <dn>He</dn> who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of <dn>His</dn> flock? Where is <dn>He</dn> who put <dn>His</dn> Set-apart Spirit within him, [12] who led them by the right hand of Mosheh, with <dn>His</dn> comely arm, dividing the water before them to make for <dn>Himself</dn> an everlasting Name, [13] who led them through the deep? Like a horse in the wilderness they did not stumble.” [14] As a beast goes down into the valley, and the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> causes him to rest, so <dn>You</dn> led <dn>Your</dn> people, to make <dn>Yourself</dn> a comely Name.
